summary: Iteration 5 re-verifies audio no-overlap invariant across BOTH directions after the reported STOP-direction fix (stopAmbient/toggle-off resume app ambience INSIDE fadeTo onDone). Frontend-only test. Instrumented HTMLMediaElement.play + window.Audio constructor via page.add_init_script, sampled every 20ms across 11 phases. Used pushState+popstate for SPA navigation (the goto('/oeuvre/:id') on a fresh page was resetting __samples because the instrumentation ran again on the new document; switched to a single goto('/') then SPA nav preserved all samples). Real WAV uploads on TEST_I5c_Amb + TEST_I5c_Cre. RESULTS: A_LAUNCH=0ms, A_STEADY=0ms (max_concurrent=1), B_STOP=240ms OVERLAP (12 ticks x 20ms) max_concurrent=2 — THE SUPPOSEDLY-FIXED PATH IS STILL BROKEN, B_STEADY=0ms, C_RELAUNCH=0ms, C_STEADY=0ms, D_UNMOUNT=0ms max_concurrent=1, D_STEADY=0ms, E_IDLE (home)=0ms, E_IDLE_DETAIL (detail w/ app ambience alone)=0ms, SETUP_STOP (initial toggle-off of auto-launched creation music on Detail mount)=240ms OVERLAP max=2 (same bug path). Fade IS happening (240ms is 12 ticks x 20ms during the 250ms fade). App-ambience autoplay after a single click gesture works (GESTURE→E_IDLE both show 1 concurrent playing). Cleanup: TEST_I5* creation + ambience deleted.

ui_bugs.issue: STOP direction STILL has ~240ms overlap between cardAudio (fading out) and appAudio (fully playing). The fix (moving startAppAmbience() inside fadeTo onDone) is defeated by the window-level 'click' listener in AppContext line 100-103: the same click that triggers the toggle-off bubbles up to window, kick() reads cardActiveRef.current===false (which was set synchronously at the top of the toggle-off branch), and starts appAmbience IMMEDIATELY — while cardAudio is still fading out over 250ms. The onDone callback later calls startAppAmbience() again, which is a no-op because appAmbience is already playing.

action_items: Fix STOP-direction overlap: do NOT set cardActiveRef.current=false synchronously at the top of stopAmbient / playAmbient toggle-off. Instead, set it to false INSIDE the fadeTo onDone callback (right before a.pause() and startAppAmbience()). This way the window-level 'click' kick() listener that fires from the same click event will still see cardActiveRef===true and no-op.
Alternative: in kick()/startAppAmbience(), also guard with `!cardAudio.current || cardAudio.current.paused` in addition to cardActiveRef.

Alternative 2: the window-level click listener could be gated behind a 'has ever played' ref — once the first successful app-ambience play happened, unregister the kick listeners entirely (they exist only to satisfy autoplay policy on first user gesture).
critical_code_review_comments: AppContext.js line 100-103 window-level pointerdown/click/keydown/touchstart listener fires for EVERY interaction app-wide including the click that triggers playAmbient toggle-off. This is the direct cause of the STOP-direction overlap.

cardActiveRef.current is a synchronous latch, but it's set to false at the START of the STOP transition (line 128 in playAmbient toggle-off, line 146 in stopAmbient) — while the audio is still audibly playing. The invariant 'cardActiveRef===true iff cardAudio is currently owning the channel' is violated during the 250ms fade window.
playAmbient toggle-off (line 127-131) also calls `a.pause()` inside the onDone but doesn't reset a.currentTime — inconsistent with stopAmbient which resets currentTime. Minor.
SETUP_STOP phase (the initial user click to toggle off the auto-launched creation music on Detail mount) exhibits the same 240ms overlap — confirming it's the STOP path (not RELAUNCH) that's broken.

success_rate.frontend: 9/11 phases pass. FAIL: SETUP_STOP=240ms, B_STOP=240ms. All other phases (LAUNCH, STEADY, RELAUNCH, UNMOUNT, IDLE) = 0ms overlap.

seed_data_creation: Created + deleted per run: TEST_I5c_Amb (ambience with tiny 1s 440Hz WAV) and TEST_I5c_Cre (creation category=manga with tiny 1s 660Hz WAV). Both cleaned up via DELETE /api/creations/:id and /api/ambiences/:id.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To reproduce: (1) inject add_init_script that hooks HTMLMediaElement.prototype.play + wraps window.Audio and pushes {phase,n} every 20ms where n=count of audios with paused===false; (2) do a SINGLE page.goto('/') then use `window.history.pushState({}, '', '/oeuvre/<cre>'); window.dispatchEvent(new PopStateEvent('popstate'))` to SPA-nav to detail — DO NOT call page.goto('/oeuvre/:id') because init_script re-runs on new document and wipes __samples; (3) exercise LAUNCH/STOP/RELAUNCH via clicking [data-testid="detail-ambient"] and UNMOUNT via [data-testid="detail-back"]. The STOP direction (both stopAmbient AND playAmbient toggle-off) currently produces ~240ms of dual-audio overlap because the window-level click listener installed by AppContext synchronously kicks startAppAmbience() the moment cardActiveRef flips to false — the fadeTo onDone-based fix doesn't defeat this racing global listener. UNMOUNT path is clean because it goes via nav(-1) → useEffect cleanup which runs stopAmbient AFTER the click event has fully bubbled.
rca of the issue: Bug: B_STOP phase (creation music toggle-off resuming app ambience) still shows ~240ms overlap where both <audio> elements have paused===false — exactly the duration of the 250ms fadeTo. RCA: AppContext.js line 100-103 registers window-level 'click'/'pointerdown'/'keydown'/'touchstart' listeners that call kick() → startAppAmbience() whenever cardActiveRef.current===false. In the STOP path (both stopAmbient at line 144 and the playAmbient toggle-off branch at line 127), cardActiveRef.current is set to false SYNCHRONOUSLY before the fadeTo begins. The click event that triggered the toggle-off then continues bubbling to window; the window 'click' listener reads the now-false cardActiveRef and immediately calls startAppAmbience() → appAudio.play() → appAudio.paused becomes false right away, while cardAudio is still 250ms into its fade with paused===false. Result: 12 sample ticks (~240ms) of dual audios paused===false, contradicting the 'NEVER two musics playing simultaneously' invariant. UNMOUNT path (D_UNMOUNT) is clean because it fires stopAmbient from a React useEffect cleanup which runs AFTER the click event bubble phase completes — so the racing kick() at bubble time still sees cardActiveRef===true and no-ops. Fix: move `cardActiveRef.current = false` from the top of the STOP branches to INSIDE the fadeTo onDone callback (right next to `a.pause()` and `startAppAmbience()`). Alternatively, make kick()/startAppAmbience() also require `cardAudio.current.paused === true` before proceeding.
